name: Taiwan independence movement
summary: The Taiwan independence movement holds that Taiwan is, or should become, a sovereign state that is not part of the People's Republic of China and that only the people living in Taiwan may decide its status, by referendum if needed. It grew out of opposition to Kuomintang martial law, ties a civic, multi-ethnic Taiwanese identity to democracy, and divides between deep green advocates of a new Republic of Taiwan and light green adherents who hold the ROC on Taiwan already independent.
scope: The national question only: sovereignty, territory, identity, language, culture, minorities and the means accepted. Drawn from the 1964 Declaration of Formosan Self-Salvation, Li Thian-hok (1958), the DPP's main propositions, 1999 Resolution on Taiwan's Future, 2004 and 2007 resolutions, the 1999 China white paper and the Lee, Chen, Tsai and Lai statements. The DPP's economic, welfare, social and general foreign policy are borrowing and are left null. Pro-unification and fringe ethnic strands are excluded.

national-self-determination.rationale: The DPP platform founds its case on the people's right of self-determination, Peng and WUFI's mission rest independence on it, and Chen (2002) says only Taiwan's 23 million people may decide its status.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The platform says Taiwan's residents decide its political belonging by referendum, and Chen (2002) calls a referendum a basic human right of the 23 million people when Taiwan's status is at issue.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The platform says the people are the source of state power, the 1964 Declaration rejects a regime that represents no one, and Chen's 2000 inaugural says the country belongs to the people.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The platform opposes seizing territory by occupation or conquest and says no government may decide Taiwan's belonging for its residents; the 2004 resolution frames resisting annexation as the present task.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The platform and the 1999 resolution oppose force in settling disputes and deny any government the power to decide Taiwan's status over its residents, rejecting coercion to keep Taiwan in China.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The 1999 resolution limits Taiwan's jurisdiction to Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu and their waters, and the platform says its sovereignty does not extend to mainland China and opposes conquest.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Peng holds that peoples of similar origin, religion, culture and language may rightly form separate states, and the DPP texts accept shared ancestry with China while holding the two states separate.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Peng says modern nation-states rest on a sense of common destiny, not on ancestry, culture, religion or language, and Chen's 2004 inaugural aims to transcend the limits of ethnicity, lineage, language and culture; the 1964 Declaration says any people with shared interests may form a state.

civilizational-union.rationale: Peng says affinities of culture or religion give no claim to political union, that one can be proud of Chinese heritage and still be politically separate, and the DPP texts reject union despite a shared cultural heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 2004 resolution condemns successive foreign regimes' rule over Taiwan as colonial, and the UFI charter rejects all authoritarian dictatorship and colonial rule.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The 1964 Declaration sets self-defence as the principle for the armed forces and rejects the offensive 'reconquer the mainland' war as impossible.

democracy-best.rationale: The platform builds the new state on a free democratic order resting on the majority's free will, and the 2004 resolution roots Taiwanese identity in the struggle for democracy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1964 Declaration demands a head of state chosen by universal suffrage, and the resolutions and Lai's 2024 address treat the 1996 direct presidential election as marking Taiwan's sovereignty.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration calls for a head of state elected by universal suffrage and the platform makes the people the source of all state power.

indirect-election.rationale: The Declaration asks for popular election of the head of state and the resolutions celebrate the full re-election of parliament and the direct presidential vote.

one-party-rule.rationale: The platform opposes any one-party dictatorship and asks for freedom and equality of political parties; the Declaration demands legal standing for opposition parties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Declaration demands freedom of assembly and association and legal status for opposition parties, and the platform protects freedom of association and prohibits persecution of dissidents.

party-controls-media.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1964 Declaration calls for a government answerable to parliament, a head of state supervised by it and an independent judiciary.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The 1964 Declaration condemns the use of emergency to set aside the constitution and the law, and demands a ban on illegal arrest, trial and punishment.

strong-leader.rationale: The 1964 Declaration says the head of state should not be a worshipped idol or an all-powerful leader but a public servant under parliament's control.

leader-cult.rationale: The Declaration rejects an idolised leader beyond criticism, and the 2007 resolution calls for removing the political remnants of the authoritarian past.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The platform makes the people the source of all state power, and the Declaration calls for a head of state elected by universal suffrage, which leaves no place for a hereditary monarch.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The platform and Declaration put the head of state under popular election and parliamentary control, so succession by a child of the leader contradicts them.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A head of state regarded as sacred and of divine descent contradicts the Declaration's picture of an unworshipped public servant and the platform's popular sovereignty.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

clerical-rule.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

person-over-state.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Establishing a sovereign state and a new constitution is the movement's central aim.

revolution-justified.rationale: Split: the 1964 Declaration called for overthrowing the KMT regime, while the DPP platform says no political dispute should be settled by revolutionary means.

political-violence-never.rationale: The platform rules out violent means but keeps a right of resistance and self-defence, and the 1964 Declaration called for overthrowing the regime; neither settles 'never'.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 2004 resolution says discriminatory speech or acts against any ethnic group should be condemned and sanctioned.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The 2007 resolution commits the movement to transitional justice: investigating the truth of the White Terror, restoring justice to victims and recovering illegitimate assets.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The 2007 resolution calls for removing the political remnants of the authoritarian past as part of transitional justice.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The 2004 resolution says Taiwanese identity rests on civic awareness and that every ethnic group is a master of Taiwan; Peng and Chen (2004) hold that the nation rests on a shared destiny, not on ethnic descent.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The 2004 resolution calls ethnic and cultural diversity an asset and says national unity is woven from diversity ('unity within diversity').

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The 2004 resolution abandons assimilation policies for multiculturalism and welcomes mainland and other foreign-born immigrants who call Taiwan home, rejecting xenophobia toward newcomers.

single-official-language.rationale: The platform says compulsory education should not be monolingual and should respect every ethnic group's language; the 2004 resolution says every native language is a language of Taiwan.

minority-language-support.rationale: The platform promotes mother-tongue education and respect for the language of every ethnic group, and the 2004 resolution commits the government to support each group's language and culture.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The 2007 resolution commits to Taiwan-centric curricula at all school levels, and the 1999 resolution records adding local content and Taiwanese history to teaching materials.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The 2007 resolution commits the party to build Taiwanese identity by supporting local cultures and native languages, and the Statebuilding Party's platform pledges to protect Taiwan's multicultural heritage.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Stated only in the DPP platform's general programme (democratic order, defence, culture), not in the movement's texts as part of the national cause; left null as borrowing under the scope rule.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The platform calls for self-rule regions for Taiwan's indigenous peoples and reserved lands to protect their living space, and Tsai's 2016 address promises indigenous autonomous governance.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The platform's indigenous self-rule regions safeguard cultural autonomy and the 2004 resolution commits the state to help each ethnic group develop and pass on its culture.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The 2004 resolution says every ethnic group is a master of Taiwan and none should be superior, which excludes rule by one group over others.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The 2004 resolution calls for reflecting on the persecution and Han domination of Taiwan's ethnic groups and restoring dignity to the victimised groups, and Tsai promises an apologetic approach to indigenous issues.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The platform opposes racial discrimination and the 2004 resolution says ethnic discrimination must be condemned and every group's equality protected.

racial-franchise.rationale: The platform makes all residents the decision-makers of Taiwan's future and the 2004 resolution makes every ethnic group a master of Taiwan.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The 2004 resolution condemns ethnic discrimination and calls for more interaction between ethnic groups to improve relations.

population-transfer.rationale: The 2004 resolution says mainland Chinese immigrants must not be collectively blamed for the KMT's repression and that every ethnic group is a master of Taiwan.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 2004 resolution attributes repression to a few KMT leaders, not any ethnic group, and rejects collective blame of an ethnic group.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The platform says all are equal before the law and protects human dignity, and the 2004 resolution protects the equality and dignity of every ethnic group.

missingStatements.text: A state should drop constitutional claims to territory it does not actually govern.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1999 resolution limits Taiwan's jurisdiction to Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu and their waters, and the platform says its sovereignty does not encompass mainland China and calls for redefining territory.

missingStatements.text: A country freed from authoritarian rule should replace the constitution that rule left behind with a new one.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1964 Declaration calls for a newly drafted constitution, and the platform and the 2007 resolution call for a new constitution in place of the Five-Power ROC constitution.

notes: Searched: sovereignty and territory, identity, language and culture, minorities and indigenous peoples, transitional justice, democratic institutions, defence and force, nuclear weapons. Economy, welfare, labour, taxation, ecology, nuclear power, gender, family, religion and general foreign policy appear only in the DPP's general programme or not at all, so they are null under the scope rule. The 1964 Declaration also carries a progressive-tax programme, left null as a 1964 programme item not restated by the movement. Deep green strands (a new Republic of Taiwan) and light green strands (the ROC already independent) agree on the answers given. Not reached: a full Lee Teng-hui or Chen Shui-bian speech corpus, and the Taiwan Solidarity Union or World United Formosans for Independence platforms. Review (2026-10-30): answers resting only on the DPP platform's principles 2-6 and action guidelines (democratic order, defence, culture) are null as party programme; democratic-order answers are kept where the 1964 Declaration or the national resolutions state them. Violence: a documented split (0 low) on revolution, null on 'never'. Deepen pass (2026-10-30): read Peng's A Taste of Freedom in full text (ch. 13 holds his statement of nation and self-determination), Chen Shui-bian's 2000 and 2004 inaugurals and his 2002 'one country on each side' address, the UFI 1958 charter and WUFI mission, the 2007 normalization resolution, the Statebuilding Party platform. Not found as text: the Taiwan Solidarity Union founding platform, Peng's 1996 campaign speeches, a WUFI charter beyond its mission, TAUP and Taiwan Statebuilding Party platforms in English (TSP's Chinese platform read), the 2007 'four wants' speech text (CNA reports only). Strands: the Statebuilding Party says sovereignty needs no unification-independence vote, and Chen's 2000 inaugural pledged not to promote such a referendum while Beijing renounces force, yet the principle that Taiwan's people decide is common to all.
